Sedjem 0.3.5 fixes a security weakness. On a computer that several user accounts share, a program that another
account runs could use Sedjem's local server, and with it your transcriptions, recordings, settings and keys
([GHSA-9jgj-32cp-hhq3](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/security/advisories/GHSA-9jgj-32cp-hhq3)).
Every request to the server now needs a secret that only your own window has. A computer with one user account was
not affected, and nothing was reachable from the network.

## Download

- Windows 10 and 11: `Sedjem-0.3.5-setup.exe` installs for your user, without admin rights. It isn't
  signed yet, so SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
  Installing over 0.3.4 keeps your transcriptions, keys and models.
- Linux (x64): unpack `Sedjem-0.3.5-linux-x64.tar.gz` and run `Sedjem/Sedjem`.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of both.

0.3.4 can update itself: *Settings → Updates*, then *Update now*. Sedjem then opens again in a new window, and the
window that was open can be closed; after two minutes it says that Sedjem didn't come back.

## What changes when you use it

- Sedjem takes a new port and a new secret each time it starts, so its address changes. `./app.sh` and the desktop
  app open it for you. A bookmark of the address no longer works, and a window opened at the address alone says how
  to open Sedjem. To open it in another browser, open `open-sedjem.html` in the data folder, which *Settings* shows
  under *Your data*; `./app.sh` also names the file when it starts.
- `./app.sh` opens Sedjem in a window with a browser profile of its own when Edge, Chrome, Chromium or Brave is
  installed, else in your default browser.
- The theme, the library's order and the video size start from their defaults once. Sedjem now keeps them in the
  data folder, so they stay from one start to the next.
- Sedjem no longer offers to be installed as a web app. If you installed it that way, remove that app: it opens
  the old address, `127.0.0.1:8765`.
- After *Update now*, Sedjem opens again in a new window, and the window that was open says so.
- Scripts that call the API send the secret in `session.key` in the data folder as the `X-Sedjem-Token` header, to
  the port in `port` there
  ([the app's API](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/sedjem/blob/main/docs/09-app.md#api-for-scripts)).
  `--port` or `[server] port` still fixes the port.

## Server

- It listens only on this computer, and says why it won't start on another host (#120).

## Under the hood

- transcribe-cpp 0.4.2, which gave the same transcript of a real recording as 0.4.1 (#115), and three updated Python
  packages (#116).

## Docs

- A security policy, with how to report a vulnerability privately (#121), and a threat model of the keys, remote
  runs, the MCP server, YouTube links and the local server (#128).
- A contributing guide, a contributor licence agreement, a trademark policy and a code of conduct (#123).
- The model counts match `app/config.toml` (#117).

## Known limits

- Browsers installed as Snaps, such as Ubuntu's Firefox, can't open files in hidden folders of your home folder,
  such as the Linux build's data folder `~/.local/share/sedjem`. There the desktop window opens Sedjem, or a
  browser that isn't a Snap.
